    <item>
      <title>Relocation of Cape Town baboons to sanctuary ignites heated protests</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/cape-town-baboons-relocation-protests</link>
      <description><p>Demonstrators tried to block vehicle carrying the baboons, whose capture authorities say is needed to protect both primate and human</p><p>The relocation of a troop of baboons in Cape Town to a wildlife sanctuary has triggered furious protests by local people opposed to their capture, which officials argue is necessary to stop human-wildlife conflict in the city.</p><p>The 44-member Waterfall troop (named after the area they mainly inhabit) was captured in the southern seaside suburb of Simon’s Town on Friday and Saturday. A second, smaller Seaforth troop is also due to be moved.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/cape-town-baboons-relocation-protests">Continue reading...</a></description>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/world/southafrica">South Africa</category>
      <category domain="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/wildlife">Wildlife</category>

      <title>Delaware hit by rare November tornado</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado</link>
      <description><p>Meanwhile, severe thunderstorms bring hailstones the size of baseballs in Argentina</p><p>The National Weather Service in the US has confirmed that an EF1 tornado touched down south-east of Newark in the Salem Woods neighbourhood, Delaware, on Thursday. The tornado reached 160 metres wide, had a path length of 4.4 miles (7.1km) and reached estimated peak winds of up to 100mph (161km/h). There were no injuries or fatalities but windows and roofs were damaged on several homes, a large hotel sign fell on to a number of cars, and a semi truck overturned on I95. Although Delaware often experiences a few tornadoes every year, this is only the second time the state has had tornado activity in November since 1950, according to the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration. The only other November tornado recorded was in 1989.</p><p>Severe storms have also resulted in tornadoes in Argentina as well as large hailstones. A round of severe thunderstorms moved through the central Córdoba province on Friday, bringing hailstones up to the size of a baseball (about 7.5cm in diameter). Parts of the province recorded up to 73mm of rainfall in just six hours early on Saturday. Such storms are common at this time of year. Water vapour from the Amazon meeting the Andes quickly condenses, resulting in massive cloud formations often associated with heavy downpours, lightning, tornadoes and large hailstones.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/16/delaware-hit-by-rare-november-tornado">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Storm Charles causes floods and flight cancellations across southern Europe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather</link>
      <description><p>Heavy rain and strong winds have also caused disruption across British Columbia, Canada, over the last week </p><p>Storm Charles has brought destructive weather to the Iberian peninsula this week, particularly in Portugal and the far south of Spain. Heavy rain and strong south-westerly winds arrived first in the Portuguese island of Madeira, before the system headed towards the mainland on 11 November. A wind gust of 84.5mph (136 km/h) was recorded at Funchal airport, alongside rainfall totals reaching 355mm (13.97in) in 12 hours. In Lisbon, 183 flights were cancelled on Wednesday, about a third of its normal daily traffic, while Madrid Barajas airport had 155 cancellations.</p><p>After causing widespread flooding in Spain and Portugal, the system moved on a north-easterly track through southern France and then towards northern Italy. This resulted in significant flooding in parts of Cannes, some of which caused rock falls and led to the closure of roads along the French Riviera. The Italian weather service issued a red rainfall warning, its highest level, for the area extending from Tuscany to Venezia. Further heavy rain is expected to fall in Italy and the Balkans over the next few days, with the latest forecast models indicating an additional 100mm could accumulate widely, while totals close to 200mm are likely in more mountainous areas.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/environment/2026/nov/13/storm-charles-floods-flight-cancellations-southern-europe-weather">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Remains believed to have belonged to Africans or Afro-Brazilians repatriated after being flown back by diplomats </p><p>Two skulls, including that of a man believed to have taken part in Brazil’s greatest slave revolt but whose remains were taken to the United States and used in racist eugenics studies at Harvard University, were repatriated on Wednesday.</p><p>The remains had been outside Brazil since the 19th century.       <title>Proposed NSW laws to allow coalmine to increase production pose ‘serious corruption risk’</title>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/16/book-of-miracles-apocalyptic-weather-visions-auction</link>
      <description><p>Exclusive: Public institutions get first chance to bid for rare ‘wonderbook’ of apocalyptic visions and extreme weather</p><p>In one illustration, five suns blaze down on Leipzig in 1551. In another, blood rain falls on Rome in 1456. In a third scene, dated 1552, monstrous hailstones batter the Dutch city of Dordrecht during a storm so fierce people feared Judgment Day had come.</p><p>Created during the mid-16th century, when earthquakes, storms, floods and other extreme weather events were often interpreted as ominous warnings from God, the Book of Miracles contains 167 paintings of apocalyptic visions, celestial wonders and meteorological phenomena.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/books/2026/nov/16/book-of-miracles-apocalyptic-weather-visions-auction">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Andy Burnham to say Brexit ‘has not worked’ and he will sign new deal with EU</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/16/andy-burnham-brexit-has-not-worked-sign-new-deal-with-eu</link>
      <description><p>PM to meet European leaders at summit this week aiming to secure agreements that ‘could raise GDP by 0.4%’</p><p>Andy Burnham will say on Monday that Brexit “has not worked” and that he will sign a new deal with the EU.</p><p>It is the latest in a string of comments by the prime minister criticising Brexit, after he told the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday that <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/andy-burnham-says-uk-lost-more-than-we-gained-brexit">the UK has “lost more than we gained”</a> through leaving the EU.</p><p>Is consistent with the Labour manifesto and the government’s red lines.</p><p>It improves the Brexit deal and brings it closer to what people thought they were voting for in 2016.</p><p>And it passes the so-called “<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/jun/19/andy-burnham-wins-makerfield-byelection-paving-way-labour-leadership-challenge">Makerfield</a> test” by delivering real, tangible improvements in people’s everyday lives.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/politics/2026/nov/16/andy-burnham-brexit-has-not-worked-sign-new-deal-with-eu">Continue reading...</a></description>

    <item>
      <title>Monday briefing: The many stages of the UK-EU relationship – and what’s next</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/monday-briefing-the-many-stages-of-the-uk-eu-relationship-and-whats-next</link>
      <description><p>In today’s newsletter: From situationship to a possible makeup, a look at the evolving relationship, and the bloc’s big feelings about the future</p><p>Good morning. Ahead of the hotly anticipated UK-EU summit this Friday, Andy Burnham is expected to make the reset of our relationship with Europe the pivotal theme of his white-tie speech at the lord mayor’s banquet in London tonight.</p><p>The prospect of closer ties – and the possibility of going “all the way” to reversing Brexit – has been met with jubilation and relief in some quarters and vehement opposition in others, while around Westminster and across the media the psychodrama has been spiralling for weeks.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| A woman who alleges she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/law/2026/nov/15/uk-government-to-consider-changing-age-of-consent-after-allegations-against-russell-brand">campaign for a staggered age of consent</a>, which would make it illegal for adults over a certain age to have sex with 16- and 17-year-olds.</p><p><em><strong>Youth unemployment </strong></em>| Andy Burnham has pledged to <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/society/2026/nov/15/no-free-lunch-milburn-mcfadden-kuenssberg-uk-benefits-youth-unemployment-neet">intervene as early as childhood </a>to tackle youth unemployment before a watershed review, promising “a root-and-branch rethink of how we support childhood in the modern world”.</p><p><em><strong>Environment </strong></em>| The strongest El Niño in centuries has added urgency to UN climate talks in Turkey as vulnerable countries face “compounding” crises. In other Cop31 news, queer and gay protesters <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/lgbtq-protesters-defy-crackdown-in-turkey-to-march-with-cop31-activists">defied a crackdown</a> on LGBTQ+ rights in Turkey to lead a civil society climate march.</p><p><em><strong>UK news </strong></em>| Two people aged 22 and 23 have died after their car <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2026/nov/15/leeds-car-pursued-by-police-crashes-into-another-vehicle">was hit by a BMW being pursued by police</a>. West Yorkshire police said four people had been arrested and appealed for witnesses to come forward.</p><p><em><strong>Air transport </strong></em>| The Trump administration says Friday’s four-hour nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that delayed or cancelled thousands of flight <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/14/faa-ground-stop-flights-resume-airport-chaos">stemmed from routine maintenance</a>. The US transportation secretary, Sean Duffy, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2026/nov/15/transportation-secretary-sean-duffy-faa-flight-stoppag">blamed prior presidents and Congress</a> for the stoppage.</p><p><em><strong>Tuesday </strong></em>| The work and pensions secretary Alan Milburn’s long-awaited review into why increasing numbers of young people are falling out of work and education, is expected to be released.</p><p><em><strong>Thursday</strong></em> | German chancellor Friedrich Merz, French president Emmanuel Macron and UK prime minister Andy Burnham will be among around 20 heads of state meeting in Berlin to discuss defence funding for Ukraine, and to establish a unified position on future peace negotiations in its war with Russia.</p><p><em><strong>Friday</strong></em> | This marks last day of the world’s biggest annual climate conference, Cop31, in Turkey, with final negotiations taking place.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/world/2026/nov/16/monday-briefing-the-many-stages-of-the-uk-eu-relationship-and-whats-next">Continue reading...</a></description>

An insider look at French politics, culture, society, technology and sport through on-the-ground reports, investigations, exclusive interviews, debates and analyses.</description><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/</link><lastBuildDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 12:12:51 GMT</lastBuildDate><atom:link href="https://www.france24.com/en/france/rss" rel="self" type="application/rss+xml"/><item><category>France</category><title>France vows sanctions for supermarket hacks as Iran rejects 'baseless accusations'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-france-vows-tough-response-to-freezer-cyberattack-blamed-on-iran</link><description>
France will seek European-level sanctions against Iran in response to cyberattacks on hundreds of supermarket fridges, Foreign Minister Jean-Noël Barrot said Tuesday, after accusing Tehran's Revolutionary Guards of orchestrating the October sabotage. Iran's foreign ministry said the accusations were "baseless and one-sided".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">7b89e272-dcda-11f1-a3c6-81c6fc5d0dd4</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 07:43:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/7a7a3c24-dcda-11f1-9a72-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/da8f65893059c2a60634f440f726825d42694898.jpg">© Fred Tanneau, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Controversial West African activist Kemi Seba detained in Paris</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20241015-controversial-west-african-activist-kemi-seba-detained-in-paris</link><description>
Kemi Seba, a controversial African activist known for his virulent anti-Western stance, has been arrested in Paris, a source close to the case told AFP Tuesday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b9cb5c02-8aff-11ef-811f-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Tue, 15 Oct 2024 14:17:13 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d792557e-8afa-11ef-b7b5-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/000_1U53IC.jpg">© Stéphane de Sakutin, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France’s new health pass rules raise questions as many scramble to adapt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-france-s-new-health-pass-rules-raise-questions-as-many-scramble-to-adapt</link><description>
While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/95a7a1f4-e018-11eb-931e-005056bf30b7/w:1024/p:16x9/61be21e7dd8409eb6f2604b7d2e8d59f8e2865dc.jpg"/><enclosure 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macrons file new defamation lawsuit against US podcaster over transgender rumours</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261110-macrons-file-new-defamation-lawsuit-against-us-podcaster-over-transgender-rumours</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron and his wife Brigitte filed a second lawsuit against US right-wing podcaster Candace Owens over false claims on her gender, accusing her of continuing to spread the allegations and profiting from them despite earlier legal action. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">efe09190-dcbf-11f1-9487-5f60e87d1ec6</guid><pubDate>Tue, 10 Nov 2026 04:33:54 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ef3af00a-dcbf-11f1-b34e-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/cb700a478b2bb0246e753a3e44c0a699e13978e9.jpg">© Abdul Saboor, POOL/AFP/File</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20210714-top-contemporary-french-artist-christian-boltanski-dies-aged-76</link><description>
Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b7135ce8-e4c8-11eb-89be-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 18:44:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/8bb5a986-e4b7-11eb-b34d-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/e857c10696aa723e38930cb9e30ea78aa32eb150.jpg">© Miguel Riopa, AFP</source><dc:creator>NEWS WIRES</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Crumbs': French PM's 1.6% minimum wage increase fails to placate unions</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-french-pm-lecornu-announces-increase-minimum-wage-bid-to-calm-protests</link><description>
French Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu announced on Monday that a planned 1.6% increase in the minimum wage would be brought forward from January to December after holding talks with trade unions and business leaders over the cost-of-living crisis that has fuelled weeks of unrest across France. The increase fell well short of the demands of unions, which have called for fresh protests in the coming days.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f6ee1d4e-dc43-11f1-9280-633626f68692</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 13:52:34 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23136886-dc33-11f1-b2ff-a575454bc579/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6WB27W.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Paris police officers go on trial over 2020 beating of Black man</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261109-paris-police-officers-go-on-trial-over-2020-beating-of-black-man</link><description>
Three French police officers went on trial Monday over the 2020 beating of Black music producer Michel Zecler in Paris. The assault, which was captured on camera, sparked nationwide outrage and renewed scrutiny of police violence and racism in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">476e3e4a-dc24-11f1-9f04-f3d8b2b0702c</guid><pubDate>Mon, 09 Nov 2026 10:08:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/dba8d6a2-dc23-11f1-9698-695cb59fade5/w:1024/p:16x9/000-D6VU4CT.jpg">© Thomas Samson, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French students vow to continue protests despite concessions from Macron govt</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261026-macron-vows-concrete-measures-to-address-student-demands-after-unrest</link><description>
French student leaders on Monday called for more protests despite President Emmanuel Macron's pledge of  "concrete and strong" measures to address their demands after weeks of nationwide unrest. Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu met with high school representatives alongside education ministers to announce follow-up action ranging from a total overhaul of higher education admissions platform Parcoursup to a cap on class sizes.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">ade564d2-d134-11f1-9bc8-6d20ccb9a352</guid><pubDate>Mon, 26 Oct 2026 12:25:21 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0691971e-d134-11f1-baaf-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26299412584753.jpg">© Aurelien Morissard, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Focus</category><title>How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/focus/20210714-how-the-french-army-trains-for-high-intensity-conflict</link><description>
France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/19df5ade-e4b0-11eb-b526-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/Focus%2014%20juillet.jpeg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">023ce07e-e41d-11eb-a94a-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Wed, 14 Jul 2021 14:42:34 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Fadile BHAYAT</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says 'racist terrorist attack’ in Trappes marks turning point for France</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261023-french-prosecutors-investigate-paris-shooting-as-suspected-terror-attack</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron described Friday’s drive-by shooting in the western suburb of Trappes as a “terrorist and racist attack”, saying it marks a turning point for France. One person was killed and at least four people, including a 12-year-old girl, were wounded in the shooting, apparently at random. Two of the victims have immigrant backgrounds.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">72670cfa-ced0-11f1-8bc7-bb90dbb6a8a1</guid><pubDate>Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:08:26 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/d100c11c-cf01-11f1-9404-4d317af013fd/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-10-23T164810Z-311683246-RC249OASO43C-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-SECURITY-SHOOTING-MACRON.jpg">© Hannah McKay, Reuters</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>Perspective</category><title>'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/perspective/20220209-a-lot-of-french-politicians-are-out-of-touch-with-a-large-part-of-the-population</link><description>
Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/a29e27fe-89a3-11ec-8742-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/capture-13035161446203b32c2451f2.07563475.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2534ffb8-8980-11ec-8ce4-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 12:31:33 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Sharon GAFFNEY</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Macron says world leaders have made 'stupid' comments on France riots based on fake AI videos</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261021-macron-says-world-leaders-have-made-stupid-comments-on-france-riots-based-on-fake-ai-videos</link><description>
French President Emmanuel Macron took aim at world leaders including US President Donald Trump for trying to exploit the riots and looting that broke out alongside peaceful demonstrations in France Saturday for their own political advantage. Another wave of demonstrations against France's worsening cost of living is planned for the coming Saturday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2c665312-cd42-11f1-8dbc-290623bfb92e</guid><pubDate>Wed, 21 Oct 2026 11:48:11 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/43e943ae-cd3e-11f1-a182-eb48fa034ddc/w:1024/p:16x9/c32582bbad1a265ea586d82348eed73833ee7dfb.jpg">© Benoit Tessier, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20220209-tefal-campaign-pandemic-prudent-president-keep-french-election-race-on-the-backburner</link><description>
Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png" type="image/png" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f4e47fa4-88f4-11ec-97bf-005056a97652</guid><pubDate>Wed, 09 Feb 2022 10:43:18 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/2debad06-88f3-11ec-b463-005056a90321/w:1024/p:16x9/1280x720-Tefa-campaign.png">© FMM Graphic Studio</source><dc:creator>Tracy MCNICOLL</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Teen wounds headmaster and teacher after opening fire at French school</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-french-police-arrest-14-year-old-after-two-teaching-staff-wounded-by-hunting-rifle-fire</link><description>
Two teaching staff were shot and wounded by a 14-year-old boy armed with a hunting rifle at a school in Aubagne near Marseille Monday morning, French Education Minister ‌Édouard Geffray said. Authorities said the teenager's father had been taken into custody and that there did not seem to be any link to the student protests that have swept across the country in recent weeks. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">de062bda-c61f-11f1-828c-2d5a86616301</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 09:43:38 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/734d60f4-a19b-11f1-ba2b-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/000-34RN2HF.jpg">© Lou Benoist, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France 2022: The Choice</category><title>Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/france-2022-the-campaign/20220207-battle-for-the-far-right-zemmour-le-pen-fight-to-steal-each-other-s-thunder</link><description>
As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b99fd93a-885d-11ec-9917-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/XX%20NW%20OOV%20SPLIT%20LE%20PEN%20ZEMMOUR.transfer001.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">6ecf0724-8861-11ec-862b-005056bf762b</guid><pubDate>Mon, 07 Feb 2022 22:00:57 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Marc PERELMAN</dc:creator></item><item><category>Spotlight</category><title>Raphaël Glucksmann, the man who wants to be French president</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/tv-shows/spotlight/20261011-a-profile-of-rapha%C3%ABl-glucksmann-the-man-who-wants-to-be-french-president</link><description>
Raphaël Glucksmann has won the primary to represent the French centre-left in the upcoming presidential elections, securing 66% of the vote. He now faces the challenge of building support for the centre-left in a political landscape where the far right, led by Marine Le Pen, remains a major force.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/b6534792-c59a-11f1-b235-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/Raphael-Glucksmann-000-D2X49DY.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">99b61d02-c596-11f1-9bf5-777190d2ada5</guid><pubDate>Sun, 11 Oct 2026 17:50:02 GMT</pubDate><dc:creator>Gavin LEE</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Fire destroys Paris's oldest covered food market</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20261012-fire-burns-down-paris-s-oldest-covered-food-market</link><description>
A fire "completely destroyed" Paris's historic Marché Couvert des Enfants Rouges early Monday, authorities said. The cause of the fire that swept through the capital's oldest covered food market remains unknown. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">c5504c60-c610-11f1-b48e-936bba59cf88</guid><pubDate>Mon, 12 Oct 2026 08:02:55 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/ce2023ce-c601-11f1-bf8f-53993c5f1f18/w:1024/p:16x9/March%C3%A9-des-Enfants-Rouges-Paris-May-2016.jpg">© Creative Commons</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French police clash with teens blockading schools as unions stage day of protests</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-french-police-clash-with-teens-blockading-schools-as-union-stage-day-of-protests</link><description>
French teenagers on Tuesday clashed with police as they kept up a blockade of high schools in cities across the country to demand better conditions and more teacher hirings. The escalating standoff came as unions staged a day of demonstrations against a cost-cutting budget drafted by Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu's embattled government.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b23ed102-bbeb-11f1-861d-cf265369200f</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 09:53:59 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/560db0a6-bc0e-11f1-a13f-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/07e46c53e327acb7cdaffe512bca997cd100349d.jpg">© Sameer Al-Doumy, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Legion of Honour: Police investigate corruption claims for France’s top award</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-legion-of-honour-police-investigate-corruption-claims-for-france-s-top-award</link><description>
French police took a top general into custody last week as part of an ongoing probe into potential bribery among the selection committee for the country’s highest decoration, the Legion of Honour. Investigations centre on possible payoffs for awards including expensive meals, holidays and thousands of euros in cash.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cf7e5750-bc0f-11f1-9d67-9d40f7c16032</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:43:40 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/202038aa-bc0f-11f1-a14f-555a0aff87a4/w:1024/p:16x9/AP17181434246649.jpg">© Francois Mori, AP</source><dc:creator>Joanna YORK</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Eiffel Tower chief to step down over removal of women staff during Hindu group's visit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-eiffel-tower-chief-to-step-down-over-removal-of-women-staff-during-hindu-group-visit-baps</link><description>
The head of the Eiffel Tower is set to step down in the wake of a controversy sparked by the removal of female workers during a private visit of the Paris landmark by members of the Hindu sect BAPS, which triggered a staff walkout earlier this month and sparked outrage in France.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">b85f821e-bc10-11f1-89fe-7b0f1abdd3bc</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 14:22:29 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1164fca6-abc0-11f1-a24c-005056a97e36/w:1024/p:16x9/000-C79B3WE-1.jpg">© Kenzo Tribouillard, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France's Le Pen vows to 'counterattack' after top ally Bardella hit by anti-Semitism claims</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260929-france-s-le-pen-vows-to-counterattack-after-top-ally-bardella-hit-by-anti-semitism-claims</link><description>
French presidential frontrunner Marine Le Pen on Tuesday denounced an attempt to "derail" her Élysée Palace run after a media report accused the head of her far-right National Rally (RN) party, Jordan Bardella, of making ant-Semitic comments in 2013. Le Pen said Bardella, who is tipped to be prime minister if she wins the presidency, had her "total confidence".
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0b97a704-bc02-11f1-8bbb-ad34ceb9e2f1</guid><pubDate>Tue, 29 Sep 2026 12:33:58 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0a9f2142-bc02-11f1-802a-177f79e345bf/w:1024/p:16x9/191c2d6c2fa59b9137ed69f72204c81d237ccfd9.jpg">© Anne-Christine Poujoulat, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>France puts out massive fire that torched 42,000 hectares and smouldered for 69 days</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260928-france-puts-out-massive-fire-that-torched-42-000-hectares-and-smouldered-for-69-days</link><description>
France's largest wildfire since 1949 has been declared extinguished more than two months after it broke out in southwestern Gironde, forcing the evacuation of around 224,000 people and covering the city of Bordeaux with a thick plume of smoke. The blaze was put under control on August 1, but continued to smoulder underground for weeks.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">0f68114c-bb5e-11f1-a5f5-19c8c18b5c0d</guid><pubDate>Mon, 28 Sep 2026 17:00:08 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/0e7d8b7c-bb5e-11f1-99d0-11fa9f8a3b4f/w:1024/p:16x9/b0f91c8b5c330512b36891557fe227255f531c13.jpg">© Julien De Rosa, AFP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Far-right politician Éric Zemmour joins 2027 French presidential race</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-far-right-politician-%C3%A9ric-zemmour-joins-2027-french-presidential-race</link><description>
French far-right politician Éric Zemmour said on Friday that he would run in next year's presidential election, joining far-right candidate Marine Le Pen, who was runner-up to President Emmanuel Macron in the last two elections. Zemmour is campaigning on a crackdown on immigration, including a plan to expel unemployed foreigners even if they are legal residents. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">2e6bcd08-b33a-11f1-b960-e76b244d1c83</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 09:06:31 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/23bd41de-b33a-11f1-afa9-2538446acac2/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26008389563206.jpg">© Emma Da Silva, AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French PM vows to cut public spending by €54 billion to reduce deficit</title><link>https://www.france24.com/en/france/20260918-french-pm-vows-to-cut-public-spending-by-%E2%82%AC54-billion-to-reduce-deficit</link><description>
Prime Minister Sébastien Lecornu said on Thursday that France will cut public spending by €54 billion next year to reduce the country's deficit. The announcement comes seven months ahead of the country's presidential election, and the government is wary of a new wave of demonstrations with a jump in global oil prices sparking concerns over the rising cost of living. 
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">61b975d6-b32e-11f1-ab9e-b5bbc83805db</guid><pubDate>Fri, 18 Sep 2026 07:23:41 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.france24.com/media/display/1b1526be-b330-11f1-abde-1d1125ed9143/w:1024/p:16x9/AP26142371784910.jpg">© Ludovic Marin, AFP via AP</source><dc:creator>FRANCE 24</dc:creator></item></channel></rss>

      <description><p>CEO ousted after affair with suspected Chinese spy reportedly plans comeback, but US treasury secretary urges ‘dramatic shake-up’</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/megaspeed-company-breaks-slience-nvidia-jensen-huang-alice-huang">Megaspeed says it’s a ‘legitimate and lawful business’</a></p></li><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/business/live/2026/nov/16/ai-sell-off-resumes-jensen-huang-discusses-comeback-nvidia-ceo-dollar-stock-markets-latest-news-updates">Business live – latest updates</a></p></li></ul><p>Elon Musk and a host of other tech bosses have called for Jensen Huang’s reinstatement at Nvidia, amid reports the former chief executive is already plotting a return to the chip company just four days after his resignation.</p><p>An open letter that has more than 165,000 signatories demands that the company’s board members “bring Jensen back while an independent investigation establishes the facts”.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/16/elon-musk-tech-execs-open-letter-jensen-huang-return-nvidia-ceo">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <media:content width="140" url="https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/e480adfe7860e9e4439f965fe15e55a5e4ff13f0/555_0_5960_4770/master/5960.jpg?width=140&quality=85&auto=format&fit=max&s=50878ed33290d246ee0c626a144dabdb">

      <description><p>Trump-appointed judge Jeffrey T Kuntz partially denies British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss over edit</p><p>Federal judge Jeffrey T Kuntz ruled on Tuesday that Donald Trump’s lawsuit against the BBC can proceed, denying in part the British broadcaster’s motion to dismiss the case.       <title>‘Jensen Huang lost his mind’: how AI’s smartest man fell for the world’s oldest trick</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/14/jensen-huang-affair-nvidia-nightmare</link>
      <description><p>Jensen Huang’s affair with a suspected spy is Silicon Valley’s worst nightmare come true</p><p>The resignation this week of Nvidia’s founder and CEO Jensen Huang is one of the most astonishing corporate scandals in memory, featuring allegations of international espionage and extramarital affairs involving one of the world’s most powerful men. As investigations mount into what went wrong at the $4tn chip company, the saga may also become a milestone in the decades-long history of spies infiltrating the US tech industry.</p><p>Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife of 41 years in a letter to employees this past weekend, following a <a href="https://www.nytimes.com/2026/10/29/us/politics/nvidia-china-jensen-huang-trump.html">report from the New York Times</a> that the tech mogul had a close relationship with a woman US officials suspect of spying for China’s government. Huang <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/12/nvidia-ceo-jensen-huang-resigns">resigned on Thursday</a> after 33 years as CEO amid reports of two additional affairs with Nvidia employees, causing the world’s most valuable chip company’s stock to plummet.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/14/jensen-huang-affair-nvidia-nightmare">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Farewell to Elon Musk’s Cybertruck. Has any car ever been more repellent? | Arwa Mahdawi</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent</link>
      <description><p>Safety campaigners have condemned it and owners have complained about it. Goodbye to a steel monstrosity seemingly designed by a five-year-old</p><p>Elon Musk is having a rough go of it, isn’t he? The world’s richest man spent almost half a billion dollars on the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/04/elon-musk-midterm-spending-analysis">midterms</a> in a failed attempt to defend Republican control of government. Now the tech mogul, who moved from California to Texas to escape Democrats and regulations, finds himself in a newly blue state. He also finds himself the subject of an unflattering <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/film/2026/sep/08/musk-review-epic-study-worlds-richest-most-banal-man-elon-film">documentary</a> and, if the Democrats follow through on threats to investigate him, could potentially be in a spot of legal bother.</p><p>And to top it all off? Musk’s beloved Cybertruck, the steel monstrosity that looks as if it were designed by a five-year-old, is <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/technology/2026/nov/06/tesla-to-wind-down-cybertruck-production-as-elon-musk-focuses-on-robotics-and-ai">winding down production</a>. According to Musk, this isn’t because it’s an abject failure, but because he is channelling his energy into other things. “This is not a case of Cybertruck being unprofitable, as has been misreported by legacy media,” Musk <a href="https://x.com/elonmusk/status/2119691615774146614?a=pN3ISFVZZ-aU4_-TlJw&amp;s=20">tweeted</a> on Monday. “But rather that the opportunity cost of the complexity of Cybertruck is vastly outweighed by the value of incremental Cybercab production.” (The Cybercab is a two-passenger robotaxi.)</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/commentisfree/2026/nov/11/farewell-cybertruck-elon-musk-car-repellent">Continue reading...</a></description>

French actor Gérard Depardieu has apologised after withdrawing his appeal against a May 2025 conviction for sexually assaulting two women on a film set.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">514af00c-e1a1-11f1-82bc-0f0371ba9765</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 11:19:17 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/bed8c53e-0bda-11f0-8024-005056bfb2b6/w:1024/p:16x9/2025-03-24T122520Z_62888456_RC2OJDAL4NRJ_RTRMADP_3_PEOPLE-DEPARDIEU-TRIAL.JPG">REUTERS - Benoit Tessier</source><dc:creator>Paul Myers</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>French cybercrime unit probes massive cyberattack on La Poste subsidiary</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261116-french-cybercrime-unit-probes-massive-cyberattack-on-la-poste-subsidiary</link><description>
A French anti-cybercrime unit was on Monday investigating a massive cyberattack which targeted a subsidiary of the La Poste group mid-September. The contact details of 22 million people were exposed during the attack, the Paris prosecutor's office confirmed on Sunday.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">f7093a68-e114-11f1-aa3b-e18acb043b04</guid><pubDate>Mon, 16 Nov 2026 07:01:47 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/9c15b61e-7f67-11f0-b513-005056a90284/w:1024/p:16x9/2018-08-30t091729z-276704098-rc1fe83a8590-rtrmadp-3-france-insurance-merger-0.jpg">REUTERS - ERIC GAILLARD</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Harki families take legal action over children's 'ghost graves' in France</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-harki-families-take-legal-action-over-children-s-ghost-graves-in-france</link><description>
Five families of Harkis – Algerians who fought for the French during Algeria's war of independence – have filed a legal complaint seeking answers over children who died in the 1960s in a former Harki camp in the south of France, and whose remains have since disappeared.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">cb9c44a8-dded-11f1-9b62-d30335cd8455</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 15:07:27 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/d71114e0-dd33-11f1-ac87-f71d22e7fea9/w:1024/p:16x9/000-32476WP.jpg">© Pascal Guyot / AFP</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>Women in France report painful periods after exposure to tear gas at protests</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261115-women-in-france-report-painful-periods-after-exposure-to-tear-gas-at-protests</link><description>
Thousands of women in France have reported unusually painful periods, heavy bleeding and disrupted menstrual cycles after being exposed to tear gas during the country's recent protests, prompting calls for an investigation into its possible effects on reproductive health.
</description><media:thumbnail url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg"/><enclosure url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg" type="image/jpeg" length="0"/><guid isPermaLink="false">5343e1a8-dd22-11f1-9ec6-3535b33525c6</guid><pubDate>Sun, 15 Nov 2026 10:14:03 GMT</pubDate><source url="https://s.rfi.fr/media/display/12979562-ddd8-11f1-83db-3f371022a770/w:1024/p:16x9/2026-11-05T134903Z-250942565-RC2PHOAN2E2K-RTRMADP-3-FRANCE-PROTEST.jpg">REUTERS - Stephane Mahe</source><dc:creator>RFI</dc:creator></item><item><category>France</category><title>How France's student protests grew into a broader movement amid police violence</title><link>https://www.rfi.fr/en/france/20261114-how-france-s-student-protests-grew-into-a-broader-movement-amid-police-violence</link><description>
What began in September as a student protest over deteriorating school conditions has over recent weeks grown into a broader social movement across France. The violent police response, notably against young protesters, has helped galvanise support, drawing in university students, trade unions and the wider public.

      <title>French football head Philippe Diallo is shock contender to fight Infantino for Fifa job</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/philippe-diallo-fifa-gianni-infantino-president-french-football-federation</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Diallo may have candidacy confirmed by Uefa on Tuesday</p></li><li><p>Uefa executive committee meeting to discuss matter</p></li></ul><p>The French Football Federation president, Philippe Diallo, is a surprise late contender to run for the Fifa presidency and could have his candidacy confirmed by Tuesday. The search for a Uefa-backed candidate to run against Gianni Infantino has been taken to the wire, with Wednesday the deadline for those planning to contest the Fifa election in March.</p><p>Diallo has emerged as the favourite after plans to enlist a decorated former player or manager did not reach fruition, although other names are understood to remain under consideration. Uefa’s executive committee will discuss the matter on Monday and the approval of its 55 member associations would be sought.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/philippe-diallo-fifa-gianni-infantino-president-french-football-federation">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>European football body’s plan to go global leaves Fifa on tenterhooks</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/fifa-waits-european-football-clubs-plan-global</link>
      <description><p>Findings of ‘feasibility study’ into quest for world domination loom with Europe’s wealthiest certain to benefit whatever the outcome</p><p>It will be one of the most eagerly anticipated documents in football circles, assuming its contents are ever fully revealed. In September the increasingly powerful European Football Clubs body announced a “feasibility study” into exactly how it can become established on a more global scale, morphing into an organisation that represents clubs all over the world.</p><p>The study’s findings could, some leading figures in the sport’s governance believe, define football’s long-term future. It has the potential to transform a landscape destabilised by the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/02/fifa-council-members-documents-forward-enterprise-ffe-scheme-uefa-questions-governance-scandals-gianni-infantino">scandals surrounding Fifa and Gianni Infantino</a>. Once considered a lobby group representing clubs’ interests in the face of domineering governing bodies, EFC has mushroomed into a behemoth with almost 1,000 members that has the potential to supplant them.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/fifa-waits-european-football-clubs-plan-global">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor</link>
      <description><p>Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw</p><p>Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. <strong>Suzanne Wrack</strong></p><p><em><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/chelsea-manchester-city-womens-super-league-match-report">Match report: Chelsea 1-0 Manchester City</a></em></p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/wsl-talking-points-chelseas-gamble-pays-off-and-have-arsenal-lost-fear-factor">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Three Lions’ win over Spain comes in two acts: the first superb, the second heroic | Sid Lowe</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league</link>
      <description><p>Visitors take game to world champions and, though their hold on possession plummets, their rearguard is outstanding</p><p>In the final, absurdly tense moments before <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/spain-england-nations-league-match-report">England finally did it</a> and Spain finally fell, when Dan Burn had been sent on to do Dan Burn things, when the board had gone up with a 4 on but the clock wasn’t moving fast enough and the men in red kept coming back, Harry Kane had come to the side of the pitch to stand beside Thomas Tuchel. Palms out, Kane signalled and directed and appealed with his teammates to hold on to what they had: <em>s</em><em>omehow, anyhow</em>. What they had was special, but their grip on it was not as secure as it had seemed. Not as secure as it should have been too.</p><p>Tuchel gave Kane a nudge that looked pretty playful considering the pressure, before Marc Bollengier, the fourth official, ordered him back to the bench. But England’s captain was not gone for long and when he returned he was joined by almost all of them, awaiting the big moment. From there, he watched James Trafford make an astonishing double save, a moment of heroism that allowed them to hang on. Then, standing alongside the rest who could no longer just sit there, he saw the last header clear – Dan Burn things – before the whistle went. Then he and they went on one last run, back on to the pitch.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/england-superb-heroic-spain-nations-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Hopes of promotion remain alive, but another costly collapse has raised familiar questions before the decisive Nations League game with Kosovo</p><p>The Republic of Ireland stand on the verge, although of what, nobody seems quite sure. Tuesday’s final Nations League group match, at home to Kosovo, presents a chance for progress or yet another opportunity to showcase a frustrating habit of messing things up.</p><p>For 78 minutes in Linz on Saturday, Heimir Hallgrímsson’s side gave as good as they got against an Austria side who had not lost at home for a little more than three years.       <title>Record-breaking Andy Robertson is Scotland’s finest captain</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/record-breaking-andy-robertson-is-scotlands-finest-captain</link>
      <description><p>As he passes Kenny Dalglish’s appearance total, it is important to remember that it is the left-back’s journey that sets him apart </p><p>Andy Robertson may not be Scotland’s greatest player, but he is indisputably their finest captain. It counts as sacrilege, even to generations who have watched Kenny Dalglish only on YouTube, to reputationally place Robertson above the Liverpool hero on the basis of a cap haul that will reach 103 in St Gallen on Monday. Dalglish’s international career ended at 102 and the curious events that meant he missed the 1986 World Cup.</p><p>There is no requirement to compare a left-back in 2026 to a forward from decades earlier. Dalglish and Robertson are men in different positions in essentially a different sport. Instead, Robertson’s march to the top of the cap pile gives cause to laud his contribution.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/record-breaking-andy-robertson-is-scotlands-finest-captain">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>The former England centre-back answers your questions on Diego Maradona, Bobby Robson and on staying in strange places</p><p>“Have you made up all these on your own?” asks Terry Butcher, sitting in a London office in the week he is presented with his England legacy cap. It turns out dozens of Guardian readers want to pick the brains of a much-loved centre-back who was feted en route to a World Cup semi-final and tormented four years previously by the mercurial genius of Diego Maradona.</p><p>Did Maradona ever admit to the “Hand of God”?       <title>AFC Wimbledon, a failed £87m investment bid and the challenge for fan ownership</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/afc-wimbledon-a-failed-87m-investment-bid-and-the-challenge-for-fan-ownership</link>
      <description><p>Clubs with wealthy proprietors can maintain a loss-making operation but things can be more complex when the supporters carry the can</p><p>When you walk up from Haydons Road railway station to Plough Lane there is a blue AFC Wimbledon billboard that reads “Fan owned football”, directly opposite the site of the old Plough Lane stadium where there are now blocks of flats. There is a memorial to the old Wimbledon FC – a reminder that supporters can often have little say in the running of their club – on the same corner, just up the road from the new Cherry Red Records Stadium.</p><p>AFC Wimbledon are one of only two majority fan-owned clubs in the EFL – along with Exeter – but that makes running a loss‑making operation, as 94% of teams in England’s top five tiers are doing according to the State of the Game report, even more challenging. “In other clubs, the owner just puts their hand in their pocket, produces cash,” said Hannah Kitcher, who has been a member of the Dons Trust Board, which runs AFC Wimbledon, for seven years. “It’s harder when the owners are fans – you can only go to them so many times.”</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/afc-wimbledon-a-failed-87m-investment-bid-and-the-challenge-for-fan-ownership">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Union of European Clubs escalates fight for football influence with formal complaint</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/union-of-european-clubs-complaint-european-commission-uefa-european-football-clubs</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Body of 138 members complains to European Commission</p></li><li><p>Uefa and the European Football Clubs power targeted</p></li></ul><p>The Union of European Clubs has submitted a formal complaint against the stranglehold Uefa and <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/fifa-waits-european-football-clubs-plan-global">European Football Clubs</a> maintain on football within the continent, dramatically escalating its efforts to obtain recognition by governing bodies and dilute the power held by the elite.</p><p>The complaint, filed to the European Commission on Monday, challenges the memorandum of understanding (MoU) between EFC and Uefa. That agreement, which runs until July 2033, stipulates that EFC is the “sole body” representing European clubs. The UEC, which was founded three years ago and has 138 members from 25 national associations, aims to afford a voice to those beyond the established powers and has long sought to be allowed a formal presence in the corridors of power. It believes a select group of leading clubs hold decisive influence over the fate of those beneath them, including their prospects of access to competitions such as the Champions League and Europa League.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/16/union-of-european-clubs-complaint-european-commission-uefa-european-football-clubs">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Hopkins’ late stunner sends Kansas City past Gotham and into NWSL final</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/kansas-city-current-gotham-fc-nwsl-semi-final-haley-hopkins</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>Hopkins’ 89th-minute volley seals dramatic 2-1 upset</p></li><li><p>Bethune scores stunning free kick against top seeds</p></li><li><p>Current to face Washington Spirit for first NWSL title</p></li></ul><p>After a week dominated by a <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/washington-spirit-semifinal-audi-field-gotham-nwsl-playoffs">headline-grabbing stadium imbroglio</a>, Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current finally got down to the vital business of their NWSL semi-final on Sunday afternoon, a frigid encounter at an unlikely venue on New York City’s Randall’s Island with a place in next Saturday’s championship match at stake.</p><p>Haley Hopkins delivered the knockout blow at the death, hitting an 89th-minute volley <a href="https://x.com/NWSL/status/2122090637860434332">off the crossbar and in</a> to seal a 2-1 upset that shattered Gotham FC’s bid for the league’s first-ever treble. Paired with Croix Bethune’s first-half free-kick stunner, the late winner sent fourth-seeded Kansas City past the NWSL Shield and in-season Challenge Cup winners into a championship showdown in six days against the Washington Spirit.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/15/kansas-city-current-gotham-fc-nwsl-semi-final-haley-hopkins">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Ultimate 1-50: the male footballers best associated with each squad number</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number</link>
      <description><p>Who is football’s most legendary No 9? Has there ever been a legendary No 28? And why exactly does Mario Balotelli love wearing No 45 so much? Here’s our list and the stories behind it</p><p>The relationship between players and numbers is a long-established one filled with memories and fascinating as well as fun stories behind them. With that in mind, the Guardian has had a go at deciding which male player is best associated with each squad number, from 1-50. Various factors were taken into consideration, including how long a player wore/has worn that number, what they achieved/have achieved in it, why they decided to wear it in the first place and, in some cases, how distinctly it has become associated with them in death. The below list is highly subjective and ultimately a bit of fun, but don’t let that stop you being shocked and furious in equal measure.</p><p>***</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/ng-interactive/2026/nov/10/ultimate-1-50-the-male-footballers-best-associated-with-each-squad-number">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Portugal did the extraordinary with Cristiano Ronaldo. Can they do it without him?</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/portugal-cristiano-ronaldo-football-memories-future</link>
      <description><p>The captain, the talisman, the brand: former teammates and experts discuss Portugal entering a new era after 23 years </p><p>There are days football fans hope will never come. For Portugal, this is one of them. For 23 years, Cristiano Ronaldo has been more than the country’s greatest footballer; he has been its defining sporting figure, a symbol of national pride and constant presence in the lives of supporters. After 234 appearances and 146 goals, the No 7 brought that chapter to a close and on Saturday night the team will play <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/cristiano-ronaldo-calls-time-on-portugal-career">their first game without him</a>.</p><p>The national side are losing more than a great footballer; they are also losing one of the world’s biggest brands. Daniel Sá, the executive director of the Portuguese institute of marketing administration, believes Portugal require reinvention to attract at least some of the millions of viewers who tuned in because of CR7.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/14/portugal-cristiano-ronaldo-football-memories-future">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Pochettino’s Chelsea maelstrom the best yardstick for what lies ahead at United</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/pochettino-chelsea-maelstrom-yardstick-what-lies-ahead-manchester-united</link>
      <description><p>Argentinian oversaw high-scoring games in his one Chelsea season and Opta predicts his Manchester United side will move upfield quicker than that team</p><p>Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “<a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/aug/02/premier-league-managers-arteta-alonso-de-zerbi-carrick-klopp-guardiola">big beasts</a>” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.</p><p>Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2019/jun/01/tottenham-liverpool-champions-league-final-match-report">2019 Champions League final</a>. His presence lifted those clubs.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/13/pochettino-chelsea-maelstrom-yardstick-what-lies-ahead-manchester-united">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>Claire Emslie and Emma Kelly are among those taking advantage of new research and guidelines for pregnant players</p><p>Claire Emslie wasn’t expecting to be able to <a href="https://www.instagram.com/p/DRVlP5iEgRR/?img_index=2">run at 81% of her max speed</a> at 32 weeks pregnant.</p><p>Emslie, a Scotland international who also plays as a forward for <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/angel-city-fc">Angel City FC</a>, documented her journey through pregnancy and football training on social media and is part of a growing number of professional female footballers who are getting pregnant in their athletic prime and approaching motherhood with a fresh mindset. Rather than marking the end of a career (notably, <a href="https://www.mirror.co.uk/3am/celebrity-news/lioness-millie-bright-pregnant-first-37623021">Millie Bright announced her pregnancy</a> in September, months after having retired), pregnancy can mark both a continuation and a renewal.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/12/pregnancy-womens-football-moving-the-goalposts-newsletter">Continue reading...</a></description>
